title: Foundry blocker (deck-tick candidate)
description: Rules B3/B4/C1 of the operating model. A 'needs the operator' claim is DATA a script can check before it is reported: the claim, its evidence, what was ATTEMPTED (the call issued and its outcome), the CONTROL (a call that would have failed differently, proving the attempt can tell the difference), and why only the operator can act. A candidate missing an attempt or a control is a Next Task, not a blocker (scripts/foundry_blocker_check.py). The three questions are kept apart: capability (can the credential do it), authority (is it permitted), judgement (is it the operator's call).

claim.description: The one-line assertion of what is blocked and why, as it would read under the tick's Blockers section.

evidence.description: At least one concrete artifact backing the claim -- a command's captured output, a repo-relative file path, a URL, or verbatim error text. Not a restatement of the claim.

attempted.description: At least one call the agent actually issued before escalating, with its outcome.

used_running_job_credential.description: True when this attempt used the credential a running job already holds (required, directly or by an outcome line naming it, before a credential-step blocker).

why_operator.description: Closed set. Anything outside it is not a legitimate operator escalation.

handoff.description: feat-foundry-operator-handoff-schema, AC-OHS-1: anything the operator must run is DATA, not prose to parse -- the directory to run it from, the one bare command, why, and what success looks like. Required for credential-step, external-provisioning and priced-ask (see the `allOf` below), but constrained whenever present.

cwd.description: The working directory to run `command` from -- an absolute path (starts with `/`) or a `~`-relative path (`~` or `~/...`). Never a bare relative path: the operator's own shell cwd at handoff time is unknown to the tick.

command.description: ONE bare command, atomic and alone -- no chaining (`&&`, `;`, `|`), no command substitution (`$(`, backtick), no newline, and no top-level `set -e`/`trap`/`exec` (any of which could alter or exit the operator's own shell). Preconditions are verified separately beforehand, never chained into this field.

why.description: Why the operator, not the agent, must run this -- the escalation reason in one line.

expect.description: The observable success -- what the operator should see when `command` worked.

control.description: The call that would have failed differently: a control run beside the attempt that shows the attempt's result is about the operator-gated step and not about the harness.

priced_ask.description: Rule C1: a new always-on resource or a capacity raise is a priced option for the operator: purpose plus a cost breakdown.

questions.description: Rule B4: three separate questions, answered separately.

options.description: For no-consensus-after-research: the unresolved options the sweep found.

one_word_ask.description: The one-word answer the operator is asked for.
